reason: At base (before PR), REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4}, so 'Y' and 'YYY' are matched but not implemented in format(). They fall through to the timezone-offset fallback (zoneStr.replace(':', '')), producing values like '+0000' instead of the literal 'Y' or '24Y' the test expects.

At head (after PR), REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so lone 'Y' and 'YYY' are no longer matched and are preserved literally. The single 'Y' returns 'Y' and 'YYY' returns the 2-digit year followed by literal 'Y'.

At base (before PR refactor), the percent-decode path in request.ts already handles '%20' correctly via the local tryDecodeURIComponent, which decodes when '%' is present. Decoded value ' ' is returned to the handler.
At head (after PR refactor), the new exported tryDecodeURIComponent utility preserves the same 'contains %' guard and decode behavior. '%20' is still decoded to ' '.

At base (before PR fix), SortedEntry#reschedule writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so entry.score/entry.at return the stale pre-reschedule value on the same in-memory reference.
At head (after PR fix), SortedEntry#reschedule sets @score = at.to_f after the zincrby, so entry.score/entry.at on the same in-memory reference reflect the new reschedule time.
The PR only modifies Range header parsing (whitespace after commas) in ktor-http. Content-Type parsing with charset is unrelated and continues to parse 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' correctly at base.
The PR only modifies Range header parsing. Content-Type parsing with charset is unaffected at head, so 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' still parses to type 'text/plain' with charset 'UTF-8'.

The PR only changes logging messages in ComposerRepository.php and does not touch archive/zip code. PHP's ZipArchive::addFile preserves source mtimes by default, so at base the archive preserves the original timestamps.

The PR only changes logging in ComposerRepository.php and does not touch archive/zip code. At head the archive behavior is identical to base, so re-archiving still yields source-matching mtimes consistently.
The PR only modifies CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix to be case-sensitive on the path. JSON deserialization (sync or async) for a list with a nullable parent property is unrelated and works at base.
The PR only modifies CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix. JSON deserialization paths are unaffected, so both sync and async Deserialize/List<T> produce equivalent results without throwing at head.
The PR only fixes FETCH FIRST on empty WITH HOLD cursor in pkg/sql/sql_cursor.go. INET '<<=' ANY operator parsing/execution is unrelated and returns true for an address contained in a subnet at base.
The PR only fixes FETCH FIRST cursor behavior. INET '>>=' ANY operator is unrelated, so '10.0.0.0/8' >>= ANY (ARRAY[...]) still returns true at head.

At base (before PR), get_environment_proxies prefixes every NO_PROXY entry with '*', turning '::1' into 'all://*::1'. The unbracketed colons make this an invalid URL pattern, so client construction fails for NO_PROXY=::1.

At head (after PR), IPv6 hostnames are detected and wrapped in brackets: '::1' becomes 'all://[::1]', which is a valid URL pattern. The client is constructed successfully and recognizes '::1' as bypass.

At base (before PR), Series.str.match validation requires pat.flags to equal the reconstructed flags including every flag bit. Passing flags=re.DOTALL (or a compiled pattern with DOTALL) fails the strict equality check and raises ValueError, so the call is rejected rather than returning the expected matches.

At head (after PR), the flag handling is rewritten so non-IGNORECASE flags like DOTALL are honored. Both flags=re.DOTALL and a pre-compiled pattern with DOTALL now match 'a.c' against 'a\nc' and not 'ac'.

At base (before PR), prepare_steps does not advance prev_task/prev_res when a group is encountered in the middle of a chain, so recursive parent wiring for tasks after a middle group is broken. Serializing/reconstructing the result loses the per-task child results from the groups.

At head (after PR), the added prev_task/prev_res update when tasks is non-empty ensures groups in the middle of a chain have their child results properly attached on reconstruction. Four child results across two groups are preserved.

At base (before PR), when '--' appears as the next argument the parser unconditionally sets trailing_values=true before checking the current positional's value_terminator. So for args 'value1 value2 -- --check' the first positional captures '--' and '--check' instead of stopping at '--', failing the handoff.

At head (after PR), the added check verifies the current positional's value_terminator before entering trailing_values mode. '--' is consumed as the first positional's terminator, '--check' is captured by the second positional, and parsing succeeds.

At base (before PR fix), OSC 11 arriving after VimEnter triggers nvim_set_option_value('background',...) which fires OptionSet on 'background' and ColorScheme. The test's expected behavior (both fire) matches this buggy behavior at base.

At head (after PR fix), the OSC 11 path uses 'vim.cmd("noautocmd set background=" .. bg)', which suppresses both OptionSet and ColorScheme autocommands. The test expects both to fire, so the test fails at head.

The PR only reorders internal checks in Ecto.Schema to avoid an unnecessary compile-time read of @derive. Required-field validation behavior (cast + validate_required) is unchanged at base and still flags the omitted required field with a 'can't be blank' error.

The PR's reorder of internal checks does not affect validation logic. At head, casting a payload that omits the required field and calling validate_required still produces an invalid changeset with a 'can't be blank' error on the field.
